edbDesc: (EPR) or electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy is a technique for studying chemical species that have one or more unpaired electrons, such as organic and inorganic free radicals or inorganic complexes possessing a transition metal ion. The basic physical concepts of EPR are analogous to those of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), but it is electron spins that are excited instead of spins of atomic nuclei
title: Electron spin resonance
description: Put a substance with lone, unpaired electrons in a magnetic field and it soaks up microwaves at one sharp frequency, set by the field strength. Yevgeny Zavoisky found it in Kazan in 1944. Because it picks out free radicals and radiation damage, it can date fossil teeth, check whether food was irradiated, and measure radiation doses.
effect: unpaired electrons in a magnetic field absorb microwaves at one precise frequency
usedIn: Alanine dosimeters that measure radiotherapy doses
Testing whether food has been irradiated
strength: Weak: it needs a sensitive microwave receiver, but it can spot about a billion unpaired electrons in a sample.
pickWhy: Borderline: it could count as a variant of the deck's Magnetic resonance card, but the deck already splits NMR off as its own discovery, so I kept it under its plainer name.
